claims.text: Earlier work produced HfNbTiVAl10 with a hierarchical heterostructure.
The reported HfNbTiVAl10 hierarchical heterostructure exhibits multilevel chemical fluctuations.
SEM/TEM with automated feature extraction can quantify chemical and phase fluctuations across multiple length scales.
Combining imaging-derived microstructural descriptors with thermophysical and CALPHAD descriptors in an ensemble machine-learning model will accurately predict Young's modulus.
Combining imaging-derived microstructural descriptors with thermophysical and CALPHAD descriptors in an ensemble machine-learning model will accurately predict yield strength.
Combining imaging-derived microstructural descriptors with thermophysical and CALPHAD descriptors in an ensemble machine-learning model will accurately predict fracture toughness.
The hybrid framework can make predictions without full-scale ab initio calculations for every sample.
Multiscale chemical fluctuations mediate the relationship between imaging-derived descriptors and macroscopic mechanical properties.
Precipitate distributions are inherent features of the reported HfNbTiVAl10 hierarchical structure.
Precipitate distributions mediate the relationship between imaging-derived descriptors and macroscopic mechanical properties.
The hierarchical heterostructure strongly influences the mechanical behavior of HfNbTiVAl10.
Spatially resolved microstructural features govern elastic response.
Spatially resolved microstructural features govern yield response.
Spatially resolved microstructural features govern crack resistance.
Directly incorporating spatially resolved physical inputs will improve predictive accuracy relative to methods lacking detailed microstructural input.
Avoiding exhaustive computational simulations will accelerate prediction.
The proposed method will improve prediction accuracy for Young's modulus, yield strength, and toughness by approximately 20–30% relative to the stated prior methods.
The proposed method will reduce computational and lead-time demands by up to approximately a factor of ten.
Noisy or nonrepresentative imaging data, unexpected phase transformations, or alteration of hierarchical features will reduce model reliability.
Extreme testing conditions or large-scale defects can mask microstructural contributions and cause the method to underperform.
